topic: 6 strange borders, ending at Bhutan Gate in Jaigaon
hook: Your watch jumps forward half an hour when you walk through one gate in India, and nobody stops you.
title: 6 Borders That Break Logic (The Last Is in India)
description:
Six real borders that sound fake but are true, from a lake with no agreed border to a Spanish town inside France. The countdown ends at Bhutan Gate in Jaigaon, where you walk from India into Phuentsholing, Bhutan, and the clock jumps forward half an hour. Watch to the end for the one border you can actually visit.

#borders #geography #bhutan
comment_prompt: Which of these six borders surprised you most?

scenes.narration: Your watch jumps forward half an hour when you walk through one gate in India, and nobody stops you.
scenes.headline: One Gate, Two Times

scenes.narration: That gate is number one in a countdown of six real borders that make no sense.
scenes.headline: 6 Real Borders

scenes.narration: On the way, you will see a road that closes for planes, and a town trapped inside another country.
scenes.headline: Roads And Trapped Towns

scenes.narration: By the end, you will know why a simple gate in West Bengal beats every one of them.
scenes.headline: India Beats Them All

scenes.narration: Each border is stranger than the last, so keep watching, because number one is a place you can actually visit.
scenes.headline: Each One Stranger

scenes.narration: We start with a lake that three countries share, and have never agreed how to divide.
scenes.headline: Let's Start

scenes.narration: Number six: a lake where the border simply does not exist on paper.
scenes.headline: No Border On Water

scenes.narration: This is Lake Constance, in the heart of Europe, where Germany, Austria and Switzerland all touch the water.
scenes.headline: Three Countries, One Lake

scenes.narration: On a map, the shoreline looks perfectly clear. Three countries, one big blue lake in the middle.
scenes.headline: Looks Clear On Maps

scenes.narration: But out on the water, there is no agreed border between the three. Not in the middle, not near the shore.
scenes.headline: No Agreed Line

scenes.narration: The countries have never signed a deal to split the lake, and each one has a different view.
scenes.headline: Never Signed A Deal

scenes.narration: Some say the lake should be shared like common property. Others want it cut into three slices.
scenes.headline: Shared Or Sliced?

scenes.narration: Meanwhile, ferries, sailboats and swimmers cross it every day, and nobody checks a single passport.
scenes.headline: No Passport Checks

scenes.narration: Picture a cricket ground where nobody agrees where the boundary rope goes. Players just carry on playing.
scenes.headline: Cricket Without A Rope

scenes.narration: Practical rules for shipping and fishing do exist, but the border line itself is still left open.
scenes.headline: Rules Yes, Border No

scenes.narration: So a lake you can see from a plane has a border that only exists in arguments.
scenes.headline: A Border In Arguments

scenes.narration: Having no border is odd. But the next one has a clear border, and it still makes no sense.
scenes.headline: Next: Clear But Crazy

scenes.narration: Number five: a town that belongs to Spain, but sits completely inside the country of France.
scenes.headline: Spain Inside France

scenes.narration: It is called Llívia, a small town in the Pyrenees. Drive out in any direction, and you are in France.
scenes.headline: Meet Llívia

scenes.narration: To find out why, go back to 1659, when Spain and France signed the Treaty of the Pyrenees.
scenes.headline: The Treaty Of 1659

scenes.narration: Spain agreed to give France a group of villages. But Llívia was officially a town, not a village.
scenes.headline: Town, Not Village

scenes.narration: So it stayed Spanish. One single word in an old treaty drew this border.
scenes.headline: One Word Did It

scenes.narration: A short road, treated as neutral ground, connects Llívia to the rest of Spain.
scenes.headline: The Neutral Road

scenes.narration: Think of it as a Spanish island, but with French land around it instead of sea.
scenes.headline: An Island Of Land

scenes.narration: People there live in Spain, yet every neighbouring village around them is in France.
scenes.headline: Spain, Surrounded

scenes.narration: Borders are just decisions people wrote down long ago, and sometimes they hang on one word.
scenes.headline: Decided By A Word

scenes.narration: Number four: a road that has to stop and wait for airplanes to pass.
scenes.headline: Road Across A Runway

scenes.narration: This is Gibraltar, a British territory at the southern tip of Spain, with its own land border.
scenes.headline: Welcome To Gibraltar

scenes.narration: To enter Gibraltar from Spain, on foot or by car, you cross the airport runway itself.
scenes.headline: Cross The Runway

scenes.narration: Yes, the main road, Winston Churchill Avenue, cuts straight across the runway where planes land.
scenes.headline: Road Meets Runway

scenes.narration: When a plane is about to land or take off, barriers come down and the traffic simply waits.
scenes.headline: Barriers Come Down

scenes.narration: Cars, bikes and people stand there, a few metres from a jet, waiting for it to pass.
scenes.headline: Waiting For A Jet

scenes.narration: So you can wait in a queue at a border, and then wait in another queue for an airplane.
scenes.headline: Two Queues, One Walk

scenes.narration: Gibraltar is small, with very little flat land, so the runway and the road had to share space.
scenes.headline: No Space To Spare

scenes.narration: Spain also claims Gibraltar, so the same road crosses a disputed border and a runway together.
scenes.headline: Disputed And Busy

scenes.narration: Few borders in the world make you check for airplanes before you step across.
scenes.headline: Look Up Before Crossing

scenes.narration: Number three: a town in the United States that you can only reach by going through Canada.
scenes.headline: America Via Canada

scenes.narration: If you enjoy strange places like this, subscribe now, because the best ones are still coming.
scenes.headline: Best Ones Still Coming

scenes.narration: It is called Point Roberts, in Washington state, on a small piece of land that hangs below Canada.
scenes.headline: Meet Point Roberts

scenes.narration: In 1846, the United States and Britain agreed that the border would follow the forty-ninth parallel.
scenes.headline: The 49th Parallel

scenes.narration: A straight line on a map. But that line cut through the tip of this peninsula and left it with the US.
scenes.headline: A Straight Cut

scenes.narration: So the land is American, but the road out of it leads only into Canada.
scenes.headline: Exit Leads To Canada

scenes.narration: To drive to the rest of Washington state, you cross into Canada, and then cross back into the US.
scenes.headline: Cross, Then Cross Back

scenes.narration: That means two border checks, just to go from one American place to another American place.
scenes.headline: Two Checks For Home

scenes.narration: It is like going from one Indian city to another and having to cross a foreign country in the middle.
scenes.headline: Like Delhi To Jaipur Via Abroad

scenes.narration: A straight line drawn in 1846 is still causing travel headaches today.
scenes.headline: Old Line, New Headache

scenes.narration: Number two: a German town where people use Swiss money and drive cars with a special plate.
scenes.headline: Germany Inside Switzerland

scenes.narration: This is Büsingen am Hochrhein, a town of Germany that is completely surrounded by Switzerland.
scenes.headline: Meet Büsingen

scenes.narration: Germany is the country, but the nearest German land is not next door. Swiss land lies all around the town.
scenes.headline: Swiss All Around

scenes.narration: Büsingen is part of the Swiss customs area, even though it belongs to Germany.
scenes.headline: Swiss Customs Zone

scenes.narration: That means shops there use Swiss francs a lot, along with the euro.
scenes.headline: Francs And Euros

scenes.narration: Cars from Büsingen carry their own number plate code, B-U-S, which you will not see anywhere else in Germany.
scenes.headline: The BÜS Plate

scenes.narration: So a German town has Germany's flag, Swiss money, and Swiss neighbours in every direction.
scenes.headline: German Flag, Swiss Money

scenes.narration: Its people vote in German elections, yet they shop and trade inside a Swiss customs zone.
scenes.headline: German Votes, Swiss Zone

scenes.narration: A whole town lives in a mixed world: German law, Swiss customs, and two currencies.
scenes.headline: A Mixed-Up World

scenes.narration: That is strange. But number one is stranger, because it is not hidden in the mountains. It is a normal Indian market town.
scenes.headline: Now, An Indian Town

scenes.narration: Number one: a gate in West Bengal where India ends and a different country begins.
scenes.headline: Bhutan Gate

scenes.narration: The Indian town is Jaigaon. The Bhutanese town right next to it is Phuentsholing.
scenes.headline: Jaigaon Meets Phuentsholing

scenes.narration: They sit side by side, with shops, hotels and traffic on both sides of the same line.
scenes.headline: Side By Side

scenes.narration: In the middle stands Bhutan Gate, a big arch in traditional Bhutanese style.
scenes.headline: The Arch

scenes.narration: Walk through it, and you are in Bhutan. In town, that gate is the border marker most people notice.
scenes.headline: Walk In, You're In Bhutan

scenes.narration: Indian and Bhutanese citizens move across freely, with no long queue at the arch.
scenes.headline: Open Border

scenes.narration: Indians do not need a visa, and you can walk around Phuentsholing without a permit. Going deeper needs one from the immigration office.
scenes.headline: No Visa For Indians

scenes.narration: Now the strange part. Bhutan keeps its own time, thirty minutes ahead of India.
scenes.headline: 30 Minutes Ahead

scenes.narration: So when your Indian clock says ten o'clock, the clock on the Bhutan side says ten thirty.
scenes.headline: 10:00 Becomes 10:30

scenes.narration: One step through the gate, and half an hour appears out of nowhere.
scenes.headline: Time Appears

scenes.narration: Your phone may even switch network and update its time on its own as you cross.
scenes.headline: Phone Changes Time

scenes.narration: Money gets mixed too. Bhutan's currency, the ngultrum, is fixed one to one with the Indian rupee.
scenes.headline: Ngultrum = Rupee

scenes.narration: Indian rupees are accepted in Bhutan, so many shopkeepers there will take your notes without a fuss.
scenes.headline: Rupees Work Here

scenes.narration: Both countries drive on the left, so the traffic flows straight through the town without a change.
scenes.headline: Same Side Of Road

scenes.narration: On the Indian side, the Sashastra Seema Bal guards the border. On the other side, Bhutan's own police.
scenes.headline: Guards On Both Sides

scenes.narration: Many people shop and work on both sides, and cross the line several times a day.
scenes.headline: Crossing Every Day

scenes.narration: Most borders in this video are mistakes of history. This one works like a friendship, and it shows in the street.
scenes.headline: A Border Of Friendship

scenes.narration: A gate, a half-hour time jump, and two currencies that match. A border that makes no sense, in the best way.
scenes.headline: Senseless, In A Good Way

scenes.narration: Now think back to number six, five and the rest. None of them lets you swap countries as easily as this.
scenes.headline: Beats All Six

scenes.narration: Remember where we began? Your watch jumps forward half an hour when you walk through one gate in India.
scenes.headline: Back To The Hook

scenes.narration: That gate is Bhutan Gate in Jaigaon, and the country on the other side is Bhutan.
scenes.headline: Jaigaon To Bhutan

scenes.narration: Which of these six borders surprised you the most? Tell me in the comments below.
scenes.headline: Your Pick?

scenes.headline: Next: Phone Gets Lost
